extracted_claims.text: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act) Article 113 originally set the general date of application as 2 August 2026, and the obligations for high-risk AI systems under Sections 1, 2 and 3 of Chapter III (which include Annex III systems) were originally scheduled to apply from that same date.

The European Commission proposed delaying the application of the high-risk AI rules because of delays in the availability of harmonized standards, common specifications, guidance, and the establishment of national competent authorities.

Under an earlier Commission proposal, application of Chapter III high-risk rules would be linked to a Commission Decision confirming that needed standards and tools are available, with a 6-month transition for Annex III systems and 12 months for Annex I systems after that Decision, and backstop dates of 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I) if no such Decision is made.

On 7 May 2026, the European Parliament and Council reached a trilogue agreement on the Digital Omnibus on AI, setting fixed new application dates for high-risk AI rules: 2 December 2027 for stand-alone high-risk AI systems under Annex III, and 2 August 2028 for high-risk AI systems embedded in products.

On 29 June 2026, the Council of the EU gave final approval to the Digital Omnibus simplification package, confirming the application dates of 2 December 2027 for stand-alone Annex III high-risk AI systems and 2 August 2028 for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products.

Legal analysis describes the adopted Digital Omnibus agreement as deferring high-risk obligations for stand-alone Annex III systems to 2 December 2027, and for AI embedded in regulated products under Annex I to 2 August 2028.

News sources state that the Annex III high-risk deadline has been confirmed as a binding change under Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, part of the Digital Omnibus on AI, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, moving the deadline from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027 for stand-alone systems and from 2 August 2027 to 2 August 2028 for systems embedded in regulated products.

The official EUR-Lex text of the adopted amending Regulation (OJ L_202601744) amends Article 113, third paragraph, point (c) of the AI Act to state that Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3 (with the exception of Article 6(5)) shall apply from 2 December 2027 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk under the relevant provision referenced in the amended text.

AI Act Service Desk FAQ pages state that the rules for high-risk AI systems set out in Annex III to the AI Act will apply from a later date than the original 2 August 2026 general application date, distinguishing this from transparency obligations (Article 50) and prohibitions, which apply from 2 August 2026 and 2 December 2026 respectively.
Annex III of the AI Act lists categories of high-risk AI systems referred to in Article 6(2), including biometric identification systems, subject to the areas enumerated in the Annex.

A pre-omnibus AI Act Service Desk timeline page lists 2 August 2026 for new prohibitions and Article 50(2) transitional provisions, and 2 August 2027 for the requirement that Member States have at least one operational AI regulatory sandbox, without reflecting the later Annex III delay.

A Council document (ST-7322-2026-INIT) contains draft amended text to Article 113 and a related provision requiring providers of certain synthetic content AI systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 to comply with Article 50(2) by 2 February 2027.

contradictions.claim_a: The general date of application for AI Act obligations, including high-risk AI rules under Chapter III, is 2 August 2026.
contradictions.claim_b: The application date for high-risk AI obligations under Annex III has been changed to 2 December 2027 (stand-alone) and 2 August 2028 (embedded in products) via an adopted amending Regulation.
contradictions.description: Source 1 (an earlier Commission document/proposal) reflects the original AI Act date of 2 August 2026 for high-risk obligations, while source 20 (the official EUR-Lex text of the adopted amending Regulation) confirms these dates have been legally changed to December 2027/August 2028.

contradictions.claim_a: The application of Chapter III high-risk rules was proposed to be linked to a Commission Decision confirming standards availability, with December 2027/August 2028 only as backstop dates if no Decision were issued.
contradictions.claim_b: News and legal-analysis sources describe December 2027 and August 2028 as confirmed, fixed, binding application dates under the adopted Digital Omnibus Regulation, without mentioning any conditional Commission Decision mechanism.
contradictions.description: Source 18 describes a conditional/backstop mechanism proposed by the Commission, whereas source 16 and related sources present the December 2027/August 2028 dates as unconditionally confirmed and binding, leaving unclear whether the adopted law retained the conditional trigger or made the dates absolute.

contradictions.claim_a: The pre-omnibus Service Desk timeline (source 5) does not list a delayed Annex III date and implies the original August 2026/2027 schedule applies.
contradictions.claim_b: Multiple 2026-dated sources confirm the Annex III high-risk application date was delayed to December 2027/August 2028 via the Digital Omnibus.
contradictions.description: Source 5 appears to reflect the AI Act's original timeline without the omnibus delay, while source 11 (dated 29 June 2026) confirms the final adoption of the delayed dates, indicating source 5 may be outdated relative to the later legislative change.

open_issues: The full text of the amended Article 113 provision in source 20 is truncated, so the precise wording distinguishing the December 2027 date (for Annex III stand-alone systems) from the August 2028 date (for embedded/Annex I systems) is not fully confirmed from the official source alone.

It is unclear whether the final adopted Regulation retained any conditional mechanism (e.g., a Commission Decision confirming standards readiness) that could trigger earlier application, or whether December 2027/August 2028 are now unconditional fixed dates.

The exact official citation and formal name of the adopting Regulation (referred to by some sources as 'Regulation (EU) 2026/1744') is not independently confirmed by an official EU source title in the provided excerpts.
The specific date of entry into force of the Digital Omnibus on AI (stated by one source as 27 July 2026) is not corroborated by an official EU source in the provided material.
The significance and content of the 'exception of Article 6(5)' referenced in the amended Article 113 text is not explained in the sources.
It is not clear how the delayed Annex III timeline interacts with the pre-existing transitional rules in Article 111 for high-risk systems already on the market before 2 August 2026.
report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally required high-risk AI system obligations (Chapter III, Sections 1–3, covering Annex III systems) to apply from 2 August 2026, alongside the Act's general date of application (high confidence) ([IMMC.COM(2025)836](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025PC0836)). Following Commission concerns about delayed standards and governance infrastructure, the EU has adopted a Digital Omnibus package that postpones these obligations: stand-alone Annex III high-risk systems must now comply from **2 December 2027**, and high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products (Annex I) from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([Consilium, 7 May 2026](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules); [Consilium, 29 June 2026](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/06/29/artificial-intelligence-council-gives-final-green-light-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules/pdf)).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
Under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Article 113 set the Act's general application date as 2 August 2026, with high-risk AI obligations under Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (including Annex III systems) scheduled to take effect on the same date (high confidence) ([IMMC.COM(2025)836](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025PC0836)). Annex III itself lists categories of high-risk systems under Article 6(2), including biometric identification systems and other enumerated use cases (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Annex 3](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-3)).

### Rationale for Delay
The European Commission proposed delaying high-risk rules due to lagging availability of harmonized standards, common specifications, implementation guidance, and the establishment of national competent authorities (high confidence) ([IMMC.COM(2025)836](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025PC0836)). An earlier Commission proposal would have linked application to a Commission Decision confirming standards readiness, with conditional transition periods and backstop dates of 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I) (low confidence) ([Winston Taylor](https://www.winstontaylor.com/insights/ai-act-rules-on-high-risk-ai-delayed-as-ai-digital-omnibus-agreed)).

### Adopted Delay
On 7 May 2026, the European Parliament and Council reached a trilogue agreement on the Digital Omnibus on AI, fixing new application dates: 2 December 2027 for stand-alone Annex III systems and 2 August 2028 for high-risk systems embedded in products (high confidence) ([Consilium](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules); [European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/en/press-room/20260323IPR38829/artificial-intelligence-act-delayed-application-ban-on-nudifier-apps)). On 29 June 2026, the Council gave final approval, confirming these same dates (high confidence) ([Consilium, 29 June 2026](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/06/29/artificial-intelligence-council-gives-final-green-light-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules/pdf)). Legal commentary corroborates that the adopted agreement defers Annex III obligations to 2 December 2027 and embedded Annex I systems to 2 August 2028 (medium confidence) ([Gibson Dunn](https://www.gibsondunn.com/eu-ai-act-omnibus-agreement-postponed-high-risk-deadlines-and-other-key-changes)).

### Official Legal Text
The official EUR-Lex text of the adopted amending Regulation modifies Article 113, third paragraph, point (c), stating that Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (excluding Article 6(5)) shall apply from 2 December 2027 for the relevant Annex III-classified systems (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex, OJ L_202601744](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=OJ%3AL_202601744)).

### Distinct Timelines for Other Provisions
Prohibitions under the Act apply from 2 December 2026, and transparency obligations (Article 50) apply from 2 August 2026—dates unaffected by the Annex III delay (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq)). A Council document indicates providers of certain synthetic content systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 must comply with Article 50(2) by 2 February 2027 (medium confidence) ([Council document ST-7322-2026-INIT](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Earlier Commission documents reflecting the original 2 August 2026 date are now superseded by the adopted amending Regulation (low confidence sources flagged) ([Winston Taylor](https://www.winstontaylor.com/insights/ai-act-rules-on-high-risk-ai-delayed-as-ai-digital-omnibus-agreed), 0.12 confidence; [annexops.com](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027), 0.14 confidence). It remains unclear whether the final law retained any conditional mechanism (e.g., a Commission Decision on standards readiness) or whether December 2027/August 2028 are now unconditional. The AI Act Service Desk's pre-omnibus timeline page has not been updated to reflect the delay, creating an outdated official reference (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk Timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

## Knowledge Gaps
The precise wording distinguishing the December 2027 (Annex III) and August 2028 (embedded/Annex I) dates in the amended Article 113 is not fully confirmed from the truncated official text. The exact formal citation ("Regulation (EU) 2026/1744") and its entry-into-force date (reportedly 27 July 2026) lack independent official corroboration. The significance of the Article 6(5) exception and interaction with Article 111's transitional rules for pre-existing systems remain unexplained.

## Methodology Note
This report was produced by an automated research pipeline: web search, source classification, confidence scores computed from source authority, recency and corroboration, and an automated review against the extracted claims.

source_links.notes: Every link points to a gathered source.

citation_coverage.notes: Nearly every factual sentence carries a markdown citation; confidence-only statements in the Contradictions/Knowledge Gaps sections are appropriately treated as meta-commentary rather than new facts.

hallucination_check.notes: All factual claims in the report (dates, mechanisms, rationale, Article references) trace back to specific extracted claims (e.g., 2 Aug 2026 original date to claim_001, 2 Dec 2027/2 Aug 2028 delay to claims_004/005/006/008, Article 6(5) exception to claim_008, Article 50(2) Feb 2027 deadline to claim_012). No invented numbers or dates were found.
